thread:
lia: heads-up — saw a burst of OOMs on canary yesterday around 03:12UTC. attaching profiler summary below. seems correlated with a KV-cache hotspot + a wave of long seq requests. any quick ideas for mitigations?

devon: ugh. I glanced at the heap dumps — the workspace allocs spike when `attn_sparse_v2` wins kernel selection for seq > 2k. per-call workspace bytes go up ~3x. profiler excerpt:
```
# kernel, avg_ws_bytes
attn_sparse_v2, 48_000_000
attn_dense_opt, 16_000_000
feed_forward_fused, 6_000_000
```
so kernel selection + batching for long-seq is the combo.

igor: can we short-circuit kernel choice for these requests? i.e. if seq > 1024 prefer `attn_dense_opt` even if it's slightly slower — avoids tripling workspace pressure. also consider bounding batch window for long seqs so they don't coalesce.

maria: other angle: prefix cache shard TTL is 30m for all shards right now. hot-to-cold churn means many shards stay resident even if low hit rate. for these long-seq flows we saw low prefix reuse (hit-rate ~12%) but they still consume shard allocations. might be worth per-shard TTL or aggressive eviction for low-hitrate shards.

perf-bot: ALERT: 23 OOM events in last 60m on canary (pool: gfx-32). Top offender kernel: attn_sparse_v2. Avg time between OOMs: 160s.

devon: short-term mitigations we can flip without model changes:
- enable `buffer_reuse=true` across the pool (cuts transient WS alloc churn)
- set workspace_pool.min_size to 1MB and max_size to 256MB for that node class
- add a batching heuristic: `if seq_len > 1024 then max_batch_tokens=4096`

example config patch (quick):
```
runtime.batchers.long_seq: {
  seq_threshold: 1024,
  max_batch_tokens: 4096,
  prefer_kernel: "attn_dense_opt"
}
runtime.workspaces: { buffer_reuse: true, min_size: 1048576, max_size: 268435456 }
```

lia: sounds good. what's the risk of flipping buffer_reuse? any correctness or perf regressions seen before?

igor: buffer_reuse has been stable on prod for ~2 months on smaller pools. regression risk low; biggest transitive risk is subtle latency spike if reuse causes cache-line thrash on some kernels, but we've only seen <3% p99 blip in past runs. fallback plan: roll it on canary + watch p99 and OOMs for 30m.

maria: for medium-term, i'll prototype per-shard TTL and a simple hit-rate based demotion: if hit_rate < 0.2 over 15m, set TTL=2m. that should free space for truly hot prefixes. also consider shard resizing: shrink cold shards to smaller capacity to reduce memory footprint.

kevin: i'll run a simulation with the new batching + buffer_reuse flags and the shorter TTL heuristic. running on `sim-cluster-6` now with a traffic replay from yesterday's window. command: `./run_sim --replay 2026-03-17-window --patch batcher_long_seq,buffer_reuse,shard_ttl_demote` expected run time ~45m. posting results in ~50.

lia: thanks kevin. can we also add an emergency fallback route to the quantized model variant for requests that would otherwise pick `attn_sparse_v2`? that buys time if kernel memory still spikes.

devon: yep — route rule idea: `if workspace_estimate > 32MB && model.variant.quantized.available -> route to quantized`. cheap to implement and reversible.

kevin: acknowledged, adding routing rule to sim. will report hit-rate, OOM count, and p99s.

maria: nice plan. if sim looks good i'll push the per-shard TTL change to canary after we validate no accuracy regressions on a small eval set. :thumbsup:

lia: cool — for action items: kevin run sim, devon patch batcher+workspaces, maria prototype TTL demotion, igor sanity-check kernel pref fallback. check-in in this thread with sim output.

perf-bot: NOTE: monitoring dashboards updated (kv-cache/alloc/wps). threshold alerts set for OOMs > 5/hr.

lia: thanks all — i'll keep the incident page open but not declaring P0 yet.
